title: Sequences
subtitle: Lists, conventional sequence stages and Python generators
description: Represent ordered sequences, map and filter while preserving order, distinguish fold direction, and trace how generators respond to demand. Measure actual source reads and stop a preview at its requested boundary.
estimateNote: Author estimate, not learner-measured: 1896 prose words at 200 words/minute plus code/figure study, about 25 minutes; five labs about 10, 15, 10, 10 and 15 minutes (60 minutes). Total about 85 minutes. Optional shared book reference excluded.
sourceAttribution: Follows SICP §§2.2.1 and 2.2.3 by Harold Abelson and Gerald Jay Sussman with Julie Sussman: pair-chain lists, scale-list, conventional sequence interfaces, even-fibs, folds and prime-sum pairs translated to Python. Lab includes exercises 2.20 and 2.34. New prose, diagrams and Python generator extension; lesson shared under CC BY-SA 4.0. Independent course, not endorsed by MIT or UC Berkeley.
